summary: This script starts a headless Chrome browser in the background configured for remote debugging, captures its process ID, runs a PHP test suite using Behat, and then kills the Chrome process when tests finish. It's a test automation setup that needs Chrome running in the background while the tests execute.

explanations.3: Clears the terminal screen to start with a clean display.
explanations.8: nohup runs the following command immune to hangups (so it keeps running even if the script exits), and the backslash continues the command on the next line.
explanations.10: > /dev/null 2>&1 & redirects all output to nowhere and & puts Chrome in the background so the script doesn't wait for it to finish.
explanations.13: $! is a special variable that holds the process ID of the last command run in the background — we save it so we can stop Chrome later.
explanations.15: This tells the shell linter to ignore warnings about unquoted variables in the next line, because Behat's argument expansion is intentionally flexible.
explanations.16: The -d memory_limit=-1 flag tells PHP to use unlimited memory for this command, which Behat might need for large test suites.
explanations.18: This checks if chromePID is greater than 0 (meaning Chrome actually started successfully) before trying to kill it.
